lessons.title: What the game is about
lessons.objective: You can say in one sentence how a team wins.

payload.prompt: How many points is a touchdown worth?

explanation.correct: Six points for the touchdown, then the team gets one or two more points with the extra point or two-point try. That is why fans cheer a touchdown.
explanation.incorrect: A touchdown is six points by itself. The kick that comes after is the extra point. If the team tries from the 2-yard line instead, that is two more points.
explanation.sayThisLine: That is six, then they get to shoot for one or two more.

payload.prompt: Which team is on offense?

options.text: The one guarding the end zone

explanation.correct: The offense has the ball and tries to score. The defense does not have it and tries to stop them. One team is always on each side.
explanation.incorrect: Possession is who has the ball. That team is the offense. The other team is on defense.
explanation.sayThisLine: Possession changed. Now they have the ball.

payload.prompt: Where can a team score a touchdown?

options.text: Only if the player runs it in
By running or catching the ball in the end zone

explanation.correct: A touchdown can happen on a run or a pass catch in the end zone. Either way, the ball just has to get there.
explanation.incorrect: A touchdown counts if the offense gets the ball into the end zone, whether they are running with it or catching a pass.
explanation.sayThisLine: Touchdown! Either running or catching.

payload.prompt: What is the end zone?

options.text: The 10-yard area at each end of the field

explanation.correct: The end zone is the 10-yard area at each end of the field beyond the goal line. Getting the ball there is a touchdown.
explanation.incorrect: The end zone is the striped area at each end, 10 yards deep past the goal line.
explanation.sayThisLine: He got into the end zone for six points.

payload.prompt: What happens after a team scores a touchdown?

options.text: They get to attempt an extra point
The other team gets the ball immediately

explanation.correct: After a touchdown, the team gets one or two more points by attempting an extra point: a kick for one, or a play from the 2-yard line for two.
explanation.incorrect: A touchdown is not the end of the play. The team gets to attempt to score one or two more points on an extra point try.
explanation.sayThisLine: Touchdown! Now they shoot for the extra point.

lessons.title: The field and the line
lessons.objective: You can point to the end zone, yard lines and the line of scrimmage.

payload.prompt: What is the line of scrimmage?

options.text: The imaginary line where the ball sits before each play
The sideline where the players stand
The line between the end zone and the field

explanation.correct: The line of scrimmage is where the ball is placed before each play. Neither team can cross it until the snap.
explanation.incorrect: The line of scrimmage is the line where the ball sits at the start of each play. Defenders line up in front, offense behind.
explanation.sayThisLine: Lined up at the line of scrimmage.

payload.prompt: Why does field position matter in football?

options.text: The closer to the opponent's end zone, the fewer yards you need to score
The middle of the field is always easier to defend
Teams win by controlling the sidelines

explanation.correct: Field position is crucial. The closer you are to the opponent's end zone, the easier it is to score. A sack at midfield is good defense.
explanation.incorrect: Field position is where the ball sits on the field. Being closer to the opponent's goal line is an advantage.
explanation.sayThisLine: They pinned us deep. Rough field position.

payload.prompt: How far is each end zone?

explanation.correct: Each end zone is 10 yards deep. The field between goal lines is 100 yards, plus 10 yards on each end.
explanation.incorrect: The end zones are 10 yards deep at each end of the field beyond the goal line.
explanation.sayThisLine: In the end zone for a touchdown.

payload.prompt: The ball is at the 40-yard line on the offense's side of the field. How far to the end zone?

explanation.correct: The field is 100 yards long. If the ball is at the 40-yard line, it is 60 yards from the opponent's end zone (100 minus 40).
explanation.incorrect: From the 40-yard line, it is 60 yards to the opponent's end zone. (10 yards for the end zone plus 50 yards to the goal line.)
explanation.sayThisLine: Sixty yards out, a long field.

lessons.title: Four downs
lessons.objective: You can explain what a down is and why fourth down matters.

payload.prompt: What does a first down give the offense?

explanation.correct: Gain 10 yards and the count resets: four fresh tries. That is why fans cheer a first down.
explanation.incorrect: A first down resets the offense to four tries at another 10 yards. It is not points or timeouts, just more time with the ball.
explanation.sayThisLine: They picked up the first down, so they keep the ball.

payload.prompt: It is third and seven. What does that mean?

options.text: The offense has had two plays, needs seven more yards
The offense has seven chances to move the ball
It is the third quarter and the score is 7-0

explanation.correct: Third and seven means it is the third play of this set and they need seven yards to get a first down. If they fall short, it is fourth down and likely a punt or field goal.
explanation.incorrect: Third and seven: third play, seven yards needed. That is the down and distance.
explanation.sayThisLine: Third and seven, they have to throw.

payload.prompt: Why do fans care so much about fourth down?

options.text: It is usually the last chance to keep the ball
It is the hardest down to play

explanation.correct: Fourth down is the last try to gain 10 yards. If they do not make it, the other team gets the ball. So the team must decide: go for it, kick a field goal, or punt.
explanation.incorrect: Fourth down is crucial because it is the last chance in that sequence. Fail and possession flips to the other team.
explanation.sayThisLine: Fourth and goal, the pressure is on.

payload.prompt: The offense gets how many tries to advance 10 yards?

explanation.correct: The offense has four tries (downs) to gain 10 yards. If they do, they get four more. If they fail to gain 10, the other team gets the ball.
explanation.incorrect: A down is a play. The offense gets four of them to move the ball 10 yards.
explanation.sayThisLine: Fourth down, they have to go for it.

payload.prompt: Second and three. The running back gains four yards. What is it now?

explanation.correct: They needed 3 yards and got 4. That is a first down. The count resets to 1st and 10.
explanation.incorrect: When they reach or pass the 10-yard marker, it is a new set of downs: 1st and 10.
explanation.sayThisLine: Just enough for the first down.

lessons.title: Where is the first down?
lessons.objective: You can read the yellow line and say if they got the first down.

payload.prompt: What is the yellow line on TV?

options.text: The first-down marker showing where 10 yards ends

explanation.correct: The yellow line is the first-down marker. If the ball reaches it or passes it, it is a first down. The chains measure it exactly if it is close.
explanation.incorrect: The yellow line shows where 10 yards ends. Reach or pass it and the offense gets a new set of downs.
explanation.sayThisLine: He got to the marker for the first down.

payload.prompt: Second and three. The receiver gains four yards. Is it a first down?

options.text: Yes, they gained more than 3 yards

explanation.correct: They needed 3 yards and got 4, so they reached the marker. That is a first down and the count resets.
explanation.incorrect: If they needed 3 and got 4, they passed the marker. That is a first down.
explanation.sayThisLine: He got past the marker for the first down.

payload.prompt: Why do they use the chains on the sideline sometimes?

options.text: To measure if the ball is exactly at the first-down marker

explanation.correct: When a play is close to the first-down marker, the chains come out. They measure the exact 10 yards to see if it is a first down or not.
explanation.incorrect: The chains on the sideline are an official measuring tool. They show exactly where 10 yards ends.
explanation.sayThisLine: It is close, bring out the chains.

payload.prompt: First and 10 at the 50-yard line. The offense gains 8 yards. What is the next play?

explanation.correct: They needed 10 yards and got 8. So 2 yards remain. It is now second down and 2 yards to go for a first down.
explanation.incorrect: If they gained 8 yards but needed 10, the distance goes down. 10 minus 8 equals 2 remaining yards.
explanation.sayThisLine: Second and two for the first down.

lessons.title: The clock
lessons.objective: You can say how long a game is and why it feels longer.

payload.prompt: How long are the four quarters of regulation in total minutes?

explanation.correct: Sixty minutes of playing time: four 15-minute quarters. In reality, games take about three hours because the clock stops often.
explanation.incorrect: The game is four quarters of 15 minutes each, so 60 minutes total. But with stoppages, it lasts about three hours.
explanation.sayThisLine: It is 60 minutes of play time, but the game lasts three hours.

payload.prompt: Why do games last about three hours when regulation is 60 minutes?

options.text: The clock stops for incompletions, out of bounds, and timeouts
They add extra time between quarters

explanation.correct: The clock stops after an incomplete pass, when the ball goes out of bounds, during timeouts, and for injuries or official reviews. So 60 minutes of playing time stretches across almost three hours.
explanation.incorrect: The clock does not run continuously like in soccer. It stops constantly, which is why games take longer than the 60 minutes of actual play.
explanation.sayThisLine: The clock stopped three times that quarter.

payload.prompt: What is the play clock?

options.text: A 40-second countdown to snap the ball; if it hits zero, it is delay of game
The time between plays; if it runs out, the quarter ends
The time the quarterback has to throw before a sack

explanation.correct: The play clock counts down 40 seconds (or 25 after certain stoppages). If it hits zero before the snap, the offense is charged with delay of game, a five-yard penalty.
explanation.incorrect: The play clock is a 40-second timer that makes sure the offense snaps the ball. Run it out and it is a penalty.
explanation.sayThisLine: Snap it, the play clock is dying.

payload.prompt: How many timeouts does each team get per half?

explanation.correct: Each team gets three timeouts per half (six total per game). They use them to stop the clock, draw up a play, or rest.
explanation.incorrect: Teams get three timeouts each half to stop the clock and regroup. Once they are used up, no more until the next half.
explanation.sayThisLine: He burned his last timeout to think.

payload.prompt: When the play clock resets, how many seconds do teams usually get?

explanation.correct: The play clock normally counts 40 seconds from the end of one play to the snap of the next. It is reduced to 25 seconds after some stoppages.
explanation.incorrect: The standard play clock is 40 seconds, though it can be reduced to 25 after certain stoppages like official reviews.
explanation.sayThisLine: Forty seconds on the play clock.

lessons.title: How points happen
lessons.objective: You can add up a score from touchdowns, kicks and safeties.

payload.prompt: How many points is a touchdown worth?

explanation.correct: A touchdown is worth 6 points. After a touchdown, the team gets to attempt an extra point (1 or 2 more).
explanation.incorrect: A touchdown is 6 points by itself. Then the team gets 1 or 2 more on an extra point or two-point conversion.
explanation.sayThisLine: Touchdown for six points.

payload.prompt: How many points is a field goal?

explanation.correct: A field goal is 3 points, earned by kicking the ball through the uprights.
explanation.incorrect: Field goals are worth 3 points. The distance does not matter, just whether it goes through the uprights.
explanation.sayThisLine: That is three points for the field goal.

payload.prompt: After a touchdown, the team attempts an extra point. What is the most common extra point?

options.text: A kick from the 15-yard line for 1 point
A pass play from the 2-yard line for 2 points
A kick from the end zone for 3 points

explanation.correct: The extra point kick is the most common. The ball is snapped from the 15-yard line (a 33-yard kick). Make it and it is 1 point.
explanation.incorrect: After a touchdown, the team can kick for 1 or try from the 2-yard line for 2. The kick is more common and easier.
explanation.sayThisLine: Extra point is good, that is seven total.

payload.prompt: What is a safety in football?

options.text: Two points for tackling the offense in its own end zone

explanation.correct: A safety is worth 2 points and is scored when the offense is tackled in its own end zone. The defense also gets the ball back.
explanation.incorrect: A safety is a way to score 2 points by tackling the offense in their own end zone. It is also a position on defense, but that is different.
explanation.sayThisLine: A safety! Two points and we get the ball.

payload.prompt: Final score: touchdown and extra point, plus a field goal. Total points?

explanation.correct: Touchdown (6) plus extra point (1) equals 7. Add a field goal (3) and the total is 10 points.
explanation.incorrect: Add it up: touchdown (6) + extra point (1) + field goal (3) = 10 points.
explanation.sayThisLine: They scored 10 points that drive.

lessons.title: Giving the ball away
lessons.objective: You can say the difference between a fumble, an interception and a punt.

payload.prompt: A pass is thrown, and a linebacker jumps in front of the receiver and catches it. What is that?

explanation.correct: When a defender catches the pass, it is an interception. The defense takes over the ball and can run it back for a score.
explanation.incorrect: An interception is a pass caught by a defender. The defense takes over possession right there.
explanation.sayThisLine: He got picked off, the linebacker had it the whole way.

payload.prompt: The running back is hit hard and the ball pops out. What is that?

explanation.correct: That is a fumble. The ball came loose and either team can recover it. If the defense recovers, they get the ball.
explanation.incorrect: When a ball carrier loses the ball, that is a fumble. Either team can recover it and take possession.
explanation.sayThisLine: Fumble! The ball is loose.

payload.prompt: What is a turnover?

options.text: When the offense loses the ball to the defense by interception or fumble
When a team scores more than 30 points
When the clock runs out in a quarter

explanation.correct: A turnover is when the offense loses the ball to the defense. Either an interception or a fumble recovery counts as a turnover.
explanation.incorrect: A turnover flips possession from the offense to the defense. It ends the current drive.
explanation.sayThisLine: That turnover flipped the whole game.

payload.prompt: What is a punt?

options.text: A kick on fourth down that sends the ball to the other team downfield
An incomplete pass on third down

explanation.correct: A punt is a kick on fourth down that gives the ball to the other team as far downfield as possible. It is not a turnover; it is an intentional play.
explanation.incorrect: A punt is when the offense gives up the ball on fourth down by kicking it. It is not a turnover because it is intentional.
explanation.sayThisLine: They punted. It was fourth and long anyway.

payload.prompt: Which of these is NOT a turnover?

options.text: A fumble recovery by the defense

explanation.correct: A punt is not a turnover because it is an intentional play. The offense chooses to kick on fourth down. Interceptions and fumbles are turnovers.
explanation.incorrect: Interceptions and fumbles are turnovers. A punt is an intentional play, so it does not count as a turnover.
explanation.sayThisLine: Punt, not a turnover.
